dimension.$description: Choose dimensions by their intended role instead of consuming primitive scale steps directly.

borderWidth.$description: Use the default border width unless a component needs a different level of emphasis.

default.$description: Use as the default 2px border width. Choose a T-shirt size only when the default is not appropriate.

small.$description: Use for subtle 1px borders that need less visual emphasis than the default.

medium.$description: Use for the default 2px border treatment.

large.$description: Use for prominent borders that need the strongest visual emphasis.

breakpoint.$description: Use these mobile-first minimum-width thresholds for shared viewport-responsive layout changes; prefer container queries for component-local behavior.

xSmall.$description: Use as the earliest shared minimum-width breakpoint for layout changes beyond the narrowest presentation.

small.$description: Use as the second shared minimum-width breakpoint for layout changes that require more inline space.

medium.$description: Use as the middle shared minimum-width breakpoint for substantial layout restructuring.

large.$description: Use as the shared minimum-width breakpoint for wide-layout changes.

xLarge.$description: Use as the widest shared minimum-width breakpoint for changes intended only for very wide layouts.

radius.$description: Use the default radius unless a component has a specific need for another scale size or complete roundness.

default.$description: Use for borders and container corners by default; choose another radius token only when the component has a specific shape requirement.

small.$description: Use for intentionally subtle corner rounding where the default radius is too pronounced.

medium.$description: Use when a T-shirt-sized radius scale is explicitly required and a medium radius fits the component.

large.$description: Use for intentionally prominent corner rounding where the default radius is not strong enough.

full.$description: Use for pills and circular shapes that require complete roundness regardless of element size.

size.$description: Use for bounded element dimensions, including control sizes and content limits.

maxWidth.$description: Maximum inline sizes: use in `max-inline-size`, or as the cap in `inline-size: min(token, …)` so an element shrinks to fit narrower space.

small.$description: Use as the maximum inline size for compact content regions.

medium.$description: Use as the maximum inline size for a single column of page content, such as documentation text with its examples.

large.$description: Use as the maximum inline size for broad page content, excluding surrounding gutters and side regions.

modal.$description: Component token for the maximum inline size of a modal dialog, which shrinks to fit narrower windows.

drawer.$description: Component token for the maximum inline size of a drawer that slides in from the side or bottom, which shrinks to fit narrower windows.

popover.$description: Component token for the maximum inline size of a popover, which shrinks to the space available beside its trigger.

text.$description: Use as the maximum inline size of running text, the longest its lines should get, such as paragraphs and list items in long-form content.

sidebar.$description: Use as the default inline size for expanded side navigation and supporting page regions, independently of the main content grid.

topNavigation.$description: Use as the block size of the top navigation bar, including its bottom border and excluding any safe-area inset. Derive sticky offsets and scroll padding below the bar from it rather than repeating the value.

xxxSmall.$description: Use for the thinnest bounded elements, such as a thin meter track.

xxSmall.$description: Use for tiny bounded elements when extreme compactness is required.

xSmall.$description: Use for very small bounded elements when compactness is more important than prominence.

small.$description: Use for small bounded elements that should remain secondary to surrounding content.

medium.$description: Use as the default size for bounded interface elements.

large.$description: Use for large bounded elements that need additional prominence or a larger target.

xLarge.$description: Use for the largest bounded elements in this scale when they should be visually prominent.

space.$description: Choose spacing by layout role, relationship, and relative size.

padding.$description: Use for space between a container edge and its contents in any layout that does not define specialized padding tokens.

none.$description: Use when a container intentionally requires no internal space.

xxxSmall.$description: Use for the smallest nonzero internal space when only hairline separation is needed.

xxSmall.$description: Use for extremely tight internal space around closely fitted content.

xSmall.$description: Use for very compact internal space around closely fitted content.

small.$description: Use for compact internal space around content.

medium.$description: Use as the default internal space around content.

large.$description: Use for generous internal space around content.

xLarge.$description: Use for substantial internal space around prominent content regions.

xxLarge.$description: Use for extra internal space around large content regions.

xxxLarge.$description: Use for expansive internal space around major content regions.

xxxxLarge.$description: Use for the largest internal space in this scale around major content regions.

gap.$description: Use for separation between adjacent elements in any layout that does not define specialized gap tokens.

xxSmall.$description: Use for the tightest separation between elements that remain visually distinct.

xSmall.$description: Use for very compact separation between closely related elements.

small.$description: Use for compact separation between related elements.

medium.$description: Use as the default separation between adjacent elements.

large.$description: Use for strong separation between distinct groups of elements.

xLarge.$description: Use for the strongest separation between major groups of elements.

flow.$description: Use for vertical space between consecutive blocks in flowing content, such as paragraphs, headings, lists, and code in long-form text. Apply it from the container that holds the flow, not from the blocks themselves.

xSmall.$description: Use between a minor heading and the content it introduces.

small.$description: Use as the default space between consecutive blocks, and between a subsection heading and its content.

medium.$description: Use around code blocks, before minor headings, and between a section heading and its content.

large.$description: Use around quotations and media, and before subsection headings.

xLarge.$description: Use before section headings and around thematic breaks.

control.$description: Use for spacing inside controls; select one size consistently across block padding, inline padding, and child gap.

small.$description: Use for vertical padding in compact controls.

medium.$description: Use for vertical padding in default-size controls.

large.$description: Use for vertical padding in spacious controls.

xSmall.$description: Use for the tightest horizontal padding in extra-compact controls.

small.$description: Use for horizontal padding in compact controls.

medium.$description: Use for horizontal padding in default-size controls.

large.$description: Use for horizontal padding in spacious controls.

small.$description: Use between children in compact controls.

medium.$description: Use between children in default-size controls.

large.$description: Use between children in spacious controls.

xLarge.$description: Use between children in wide controls that need greater separation than spacious controls.

travel.$description: How far content moves as it appears, disappears, or changes position, paired with the `movement` transition of the same item. Components set the direction with a sign.

rest.$description: Use for content at its resting position.

popup.$description: Use for the distance popups slide as they open and close.
